rv.q: Together they truly create an ensemble show, with beautiful acapella vocals from all, high sentiment moments of dialogue and a powerful, poignant production. The adult characters consist of Headmaster Marrow, portrayed by Daon Broni, and Mr Pendleton, played by Martin Turner.
But, such are the traditions of the school, whatever the ‘code of conduct’ actually says, that he will not ‘snitch’ on who did it.

Choir Boy at Stratford East is a deeply moving piece of theatre about the pursuit of Black excellence as a young queer man. Written by Academy Award winning writer Tarell Alvin McCraney, directed by Nancy Medina and co-directed by Tatenda Shamiso, this transfer from Bristol Old Vic has arrived to captivate London audiences.

Star rating: four stars ★ ★ ★ ★ ✩ We all carry with us a secret history, moments that can seem inconsequential for others but are monumental in our own mind. Nowhere is this more apparent than in the schoolboys of the Charles R Drew preparatory school, a historically Black boarding school at the heart of Tarell Alvin McCraney’s Choir Boy.

It’s a kind of childish bickering and sass which makes for ridiculously funny comedy. Ahomka-Lindsay also performs a wonderful solo number as a soul-searching David, too. McCraney’s script does well to establish key characteristics for each of the boys.
